card.title: How a solar cell makes current

body.claim: A solar cell turns the energy of light directly into electricity using the photovoltaic effect.
body.why: Light is absorbed, exciting an electron to a higher-energy state and creating electron-hole pairs. The cell must then separate these opposite types of charge carrier and extract them separately to an external circuit, which gives the current you can use.

probes.question: After light is absorbed in a solar cell, what must happen for useful current?
options: The charges are separated and extracted to a circuit
The light must be stored as sound

probes.question: True or false: the photovoltaic effect is when a semiconductor generates electric energy upon being exposed to light.

claims.claim: Solar cell converts the energy of light directly into electricity via the photovoltaic effect
claims.quote: converts the energy of light directly into electricity by using the photovoltaic effect

claims.claim: Absorbed photons excite electrons, producing electron-hole pairs
claims.quote: When the photons are absorbed, electrons are excited from the valence band to the conduction band

claims.claim: Opposite charge carriers must be separated and extracted separately to a circuit (probe 1)
claims.quote: The separation of charge carriers of opposite types. The separate extraction of those carriers to an external circuit.
The photovoltaic effect is a physical phenomenon in which a semiconductor material generates electric energy upon being exposed to light.
